It's the popular belief here that Free Speech is a fundamental pillar to a healthy society. Of course, I believe the same.

But what does it mean exactly? What does it imply?

I'd like to know what everyone thinks.
What does Free Speech mean to you?

Freedom of Speech declares you can say whatever you want, but this in turn does not warrant a Freedom from Consequence.
You can call someone a jackass, accuse him of pedophilia, but don't be surprised when they hit back, legally, physically or metaphorically.
To be able to see and confront any idea i don't know or like , to be open to criticism , to hone my argument skills.

You can say whatever you want without being arrested. Nobody has to listen, you may be treated differently because of what you said. You may be arrested for the implications of what you said, though. If you yell 'BOMB!' in an airport, they don't detain you for saying 'bomb', they detain you because of the implication you might have one.
That and the likely injuries caused by the panic.
The right to say whatever you want and the responsibility to accept the consequences that come with it.

The ability for a group of people (society) to outwardly state their feelings. If some asshole wants to run his mouth about dumb shit; at least him having said that allows me to have a conversation with him about why I believe he's wrong.

If his stupid views are censored, he harbors those thoughts unchallenged for the rest of his life.

To me, free speech is a mechanism for the transmission, processing and filtering of thought.
